reason: The text describes a moment of national unity and loyalty rather than complaint. All of Israel gathers to David at Hebron, affirming his leadership by saying 'we are your bone and flesh' (וְעַצְמְךָ֥ וּֽבְשָׂרְךָ֖ אֲנָֽחְנוּ). They acknowledge that even under Saul, David led Israel in battle. The elders make a covenant with David and anoint him as king 'according to the word of the Lord.' This passage depicts a consensual transfer of power and popular support for David's leadership, not complaints against leaders. The only opposition mentioned comes from the Jebusites (a non-Israelite people), not from the Hebrew people regarding their own leadership.
